quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against the light or are not paying attention.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted on the road?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you become tired.
Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What types of drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What factor affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your weight, biological sex, how much food is in your stomach, and how many drinks you have had all affect how fast your body absorbs alcohol. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than the speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed limit for that road. You can drive slower if road conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides for divided highways.

questions.question: What should you do when you see orange construction signs and cones?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road with no curb, or uphill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. If parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn toward the center of the road so your car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: You cannot pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When you see these lines, passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Alcohol first affects your:
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and driving skills first. It then affects other abilities you need to drive safely.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights, it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus loading or unloading students.

questions.question: On a slippery road, the first thing to do when you need to slow down is:
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, apply gentle, steady pressure to the brake pedal.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired while driving, stop driving immediately.

questions.question: Cell phones can be a serious distraction while driving.
questions.explanation: Do not use cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices while driving, except to report a crash or emergency. Keep your full attention on driving.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: Areas shaded by trees or buildings freeze faster than other parts of the road in cold or wet weather. These areas also take longer to dry.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. Drivers must obey all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign prohibits passing.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, what must you do?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed always.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems. This helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing with flashing signals. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing signals. Look for trains and also watch for lowered gates or hear warning sounds.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, wait for other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when leaving a highway, when behind motorcycles, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Stay close behind it to reduce wind drag.
Do not drive beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead so you can prepare for traffic or turns.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers make unexpected moves.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to other drivers.

questions.question: Your accelerator pedal sticks while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, turn off the engine carefully so the steering wheel does not lock. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white rectangles with black, red, or green text. They tell you about traffic laws you must follow, such as speed limits, parking rules, and lane directions.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When it rains, snows, or gets foggy, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to spot. If you need to use windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than regular cars.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to steer than regular cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A regular car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck going 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards and conditions. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a sharp turn ahead. You should reduce your speed.

questions.question: It is very foggy. You should slow down and:
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams bounce off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work best with low beams.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic conditions and keep distance between your vehicle and others. Pay close attention to workers and equipment in the area.
